A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same DirGINE/quiver study. Their text, equations, diagrams, empirical figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification performance, training curves across ten trials, PGExplainer perturbation results, and latent-representation analyses in Sections 4–6.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds classification accuracies for larger quivers in Section 4.2 and Table 1.

M1.justification: Both versions describe the same four-layer, width-32 DirGINE, directed message passing, sum pooling, training objective, and PGExplainer procedure. Moving their equations and implementation descriptions into appendices does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: V2 extends evaluation from 11-node quivers to 12–20-node quivers of types A, D, E, affine A, and affine D. This adds larger-input generalization scenarios while retaining the original classification task, training coverage, and quiver families.

E2.justification: Neither version reports a competing classifier benchmark against DirGINE. PGExplainer and linear probing remain analysis tools; newly cited GNN and quiver-learning works are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The new size-generalization experiment uses mutation depth 6 and random subsampling to 100,000 quivers when necessary (Appendix C). The original training budgets, 11-node test construction, and dataset counts are retained; these new sampling conditions should not be treated as a revision of the original experiment.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds an explicit test of generalization as graph size increases beyond the original test size. The edge-removal analysis, subtype linear probe, PCA visualizations, clustering, and appendix examples already appear in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report training curves across ten trials and the same 99.7 ± 0.0% subtype-probe accuracy. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance procedures; its new accuracy table supplies point estimates.

E6.justification: V2 Table 1 adds nine accuracies for 12–20-node quivers, ranging from 99.6% at 12 nodes to 89.1% at 20 nodes. These are additional results under the new sampling protocol. The original 99.2% test accuracy, subtype-probe result, perturbation counts, and qualitative findings are retained.

T1.justification: The main classification theorem and case-by-case proof are retained: v1 Theorem 6.7 becomes v2 Theorem 6.1 with its proof in Appendix E. However, v2 Section 2.1 newly equates finite cluster algebras with finite quiver mutation classes, blurring the distinction made in v1 and still reflected in v2's discussion of affine mutation-finite cases.

C1.justification: V1 presents the affine-D characterization as a new theorem for a previously unknown case. V2 removes that priority claim and frames the contribution as an independent discovery of a characterization already obtainable from Henrich (2011). This substantially narrows a central contribution while retaining the claims about extracting mathematical structure from GNNs.

C2.justification: V2 hypothesizes that declining larger-quiver accuracy results from the network's fixed four-layer depth and difficulty recognizing long cycles. It also adds an interpretation of including E and affine E as making classification sufficiently challenging to encourage discriminative features. Existing explanations of perturbation outcomes and interpretability caveats remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly identifies PyTorch Geometric as the PGExplainer implementation, and Appendix C documents generation and subsampling for the added size experiment. Edge encoding, constant node features, optimizer settings, and GPU information were already documented in v1 and are principally relocated.

R1.justification: Henrich (2011) becomes central to the paper's positioning, with explicit acknowledgment of the earlier characterization and a subtype correspondence in Remark D.8. V2 also adds recent quiver-learning and GNN references and removes the OthelloGPT example. The acknowledgment fundamentally revises the relationship to prior mathematical work.

P1.justification: V2 substantially condenses and reorganizes the narrative, moving background, model equations, classification details, and proofs into Appendices A–E. It rewrites the introduction and conclusion and reorganizes the interpretation analyses. Some editing deteriorates: Vatne citations repeatedly render as 'and (2010)'.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures and mathematical diagrams. Selected subtype diagrams appear in both the main summary and appendices, and a new accuracy table is added. Existing empirical plots and appendix example panels are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves scholarly accuracy by correcting v1's novelty claim, acknowledging Henrich, and explaining the correspondence between classifications. The larger-quiver experiment also clarifies the model's generalization limits. These gains are partly offset by the new finite-type/mutation-finite conflation in Section 2.1 and malformed Vatne citations. With the principal method, proof, and original results retained, the net improvement is limited.
